title: Bug Hunt Station 2 - High Scores (IndexError)
body:
Goal: find and fix two IndexErrors.

  1. Open starter.py and press Run. Read the traceback bottom-up. Which function? Which line?
  2. Draw the list on paper with its index numbers:
index:    0    1    2    3
        [15,  40,  60,  90]     len = 4
  1. Fix bug 1 and run again. A new traceback appears: that is bug 2. Add print("best is", best) inside podium() to see what is in the list.
  2. Fix bug 2. Remove your print lines when you are done.

Done looks like:

Highest: 90  Lowest: 15
1st: 90
2nd: 60
3rd: 40
1st: 70
2nd: 20

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Read the traceback bottom up and find the function name and line number. Then draw the list on paper with its index numbers, like the picture in the README. Count carefully where the list starts and ends.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: An IndexError means you asked for a spot that is not in the list. A list of 4 items has indexes 0 to 3, so len is one more than the last index. For bug 2, print best and compare its length with how many times the loop runs.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: For bug 1, compare the index used in highest() with the last index in your drawing. For bug 2, the loop runs three times even when best holds only two scores. What could the loop use instead of a fixed number?

starter.name: starter.py
starter.raw:
# Bug Hunt Station 2: High Scores
# This program has TWO bugs. Both are IndexErrors.
# Tip: add print() lines to see what is inside a list, e.g.  print("best is", best)


def lowest(scores):
    """Return the lowest score."""
    in_order = sorted(scores)
    return in_order[0]


def highest(scores):
    """Return the highest score."""
    in_order = sorted(scores)
    return in_order[len(in_order)]


def podium(scores):
    """Return up to three lines like "1st: 90", best score first."""
    places = ["1st", "2nd", "3rd"]
    best = sorted(scores, reverse=True)[:3]
    lines = []
    for i in range(3):
        lines.append(f"{places[i]}: {best[i]}")
    return lines


if __name__ == "__main__":
    scores = [40, 90, 15, 60]
    print(f"Highest: {highest(scores)}  Lowest: {lowest(scores)}")
    for line in podium(scores):
        print(line)
    for line in podium([70, 20]):          # only two players today
        print(line)
